body.x: IT companies from the Daegu area participated in “CES 2016”, the world’s largest electronics and IT exhibition. They were given the green light for domestic smart knowledge service companies to advance into global markets with active consultations and contracts with foreign buyers.

According to the Daegu Digital Industry Promotion Agency (DIP), six smart knowledge service companies from Daegu participated in “CES 2016”, which runs for four days from Wednesday the 6th to Saturday the 9th in Las Vegas. There, consultations worth $6.925 million were exchanged. The estimated amount of contracts is expected to be $7.434 million.

DIP prepared the joint pavilion at this event and supported the participating companies’ activities by providing services for booth constructions and interpretations and by discovering new foreign buyers.

In particular, U-HANPRESEN, the company that showcased the “PresenMarker”, which can draw lines directly on screens, signed an MOU for tech cooperation and export contracts with a Turkish project company whose name begins with P.

Furthermore, NanoIT showcased its bulk message transmission gateway and conducted consultations worth $3 million with an American company whose name begins with F. Those introducing their products and catching foreign buyers’ eyes were Network Korea, a solutions developer for image surveillance devices; IT HEALTH, a smart urine and feces management system developer; and GREEN SYSTEM, a standby power blocking application developer.

DIP president Yang Won-yeong said: “Based on results that we attained through CES 2016, which we participated in as part of the reinforcement project for the quality capability of the smart knowledge service, we will continue to help domestic companies advance into foreign markets through various support projects.”

A total of 3,600 companies from the electronics, IT and automobile fields participated in “CES 2016”, which was held by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA). Various up-to-date technologies, including IoT, and smart-related technologies and products, such as smart cars, smart homes, and wearables, were shown at the event.
